hypotheses.reasoning: auth-svc v2.13.0 (build aa4ae5c) was rolled out at 16:22:47 (#1091), replacing v2.12.6. It started with 'response serializer v2 enabled' (#1119, 16:23:06). From then on, auth-svc's POST /tokens replies no longer include the required 'status' field (account-svc sees keys id, state, updatedAt). account-svc fails to decode or validate those replies (#1159 at 16:23:50, #1225, #1261). Those failures make account-svc fail /login, and edge-proxy returns 502s upstream of account-svc (#1197, #1329, #1452, #1657; not cited, since they are downstream symptoms). The onset matches the deploy: the first decode failure is about 1 minute after the rollout and about 40 seconds after the serializer was enabled. auth-svc logs 'ok' on every /tokens call, so the contract break is silent on the producer side. Ruled out: status-poller timeouts against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint (#672 and later) are constant background noise that predates the incident and does not touch /login. accounts-db slow audit_log scans (#440) and vacuum lines are unrelated and produce no errors. No errors appear in auth-svc, audit-consumer, session-cache, flag-sync, or accounts-db.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll back auth-svc from v2.13.0 to v2.12.6 now, which restores the 'status' field in /tokens replies and should clear the 502s on POST /login. If serializer v2 can be disabled separately, turn it off. Add a contract or schema check between auth-svc and account-svc for the /tokens response before re-releasing. Separately, track the status-poller healthcheck against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint (#672 and later) as a non-blocking cleanup item.
